relevance_rank_note: Abstract-level only: states that ApoE4 weakens SNX17 binding to ApoER2 and blocks ApoER2 recycling to the surface, and that carnosic acid reverses it; no panel-level data available locally.

description: The authors report that ApoE4 reduces the binding of the recycling sorting adaptor SNX17 to ApoER2 and blocks ApoER2 recycling, lowering surface ApoER2.
quote: we demonstrated that ApoE4 attenuates the binding of sorting nexin 17 (SNX17) to ApoER2 and inhibits the recycling of ApoER2, resulting in decreased cell surface level of ApoER2
summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (less SNX17-ApoER2 binding) -> (less ApoER2 recycling and surface level)
system: Not stated in the available abstract; the abstract describes ApoE4 effects on ApoER2 recycling and Reelin signalling with no cell type, species or assay given. system unknown, so the distance from non-aged non-AD human brain cells cannot be assessed.
human_check: Only the PubMed abstract is available locally (ft/31796678.txt); no figures, panels, statistics or system description. The binding measured is SNX17-to-ApoER2, i.e. an adaptor on the cytoplasmic side, not ApoE-to-receptor binding, so this is B2 (class 3), not B1. A person should pull the full text to panel-level this.

description: Carnosic acid is reported to increase SNX17 binding to ApoER2 and to reverse the ApoE4-induced fall in surface ApoER2 and in Reelin signalling.
quote: CA enhances the binding of SNX17 to ApoER2, counteracts the negative effects of ApoE4 on the cell surface level of ApoER2
summary: (APOE4 + carnosic acid) -> (SNX17-ApoER2 binding and surface ApoER2 restored)
system: Not stated in the available abstract; carnosic acid treatment of cells expressing ApoER2 with ApoE4, dose and duration not given. system unknown, so the distance from non-aged non-AD human brain cells cannot be assessed.
human_check: Abstract only. Class 4: a pharmacological perturbation that restores the recycling adaptor interaction, with a surrogate readout (surface ApoER2). No dose, no statistics, no system.
